story_type: stealth destroyer's first live missile launch, deck cameras
hook: The first missile ever fired from this ship's launchers.
narration: This was the first live missile fired from USS Zumwalt's launchers.
Its sharp, angled hull is built for stealth.
Missiles wait below the deck and fire straight up.
On October thirteenth, 2020, off California, it fired.
[short pause] Cameras on the deck caught the launch from every side.
outcome: The Navy called it a successful first live fire test.

location_card.place: Pacific Ocean, off Point Mugu, California

title: Zumwalt fires its first missile
description:
USS Zumwalt (DDG 1000) fires a Standard Missile (SM-2) in the first live fire test of its MK 57 Vertical Launching System on the Point Mugu Sea Test Range off California, Oct. 13, 2020.

question_comment: Would you want to be standing on that deck when it fired?

facts.claim: Zumwalt successfully executed its first live fire test of the MK 57 VLS with an SM-2 off Point Mugu, Oct. 13, 2020
facts.source_quote: PACIFIC OCEAN (Oct. 13, 2020) USS Zumwalt (DDG 1000) successfully executed the first live fire test of the MK 57 Vertical Launching System with a Standard Missile (SM-2) on the Naval Air Weapons Center Weapons Division Sea Test Range, Point Mugu, Oct. 13.

facts.claim: Built for stealth in open-ocean and near-shore waters
facts.source_quote: The ships’ stealth and ability to operate in both the open-ocean and near-shore environments creates a new level of battlespace complexity for potential adversaries.
